note:
R32 — Xbox 360 `RW4xb2` texture-descriptor census over the loose `rendering/**/*.rx2` trees (NHL 07–Legacy), read-only.

Each texture descriptor (24-byte file-table entry tag `00 02 00 03`, 56 bytes) is read as `DW0..DW6` (constants / colour key) + the six-dword
Xenos texture fetch constant (`DW7..DW12`, big-endian) + `DW13`, and the fetch constant is split into its documented fields (type, signs,
clamps, pitch (32-texel units), tiled; format, endian, request size, stacked, base address (4 KiB units); width-1 / height-1 (13 bits each);
num format, swizzle, exp adjust, filters, border; mip min / max level, lod bias; border colour, dimension, packed mips, mip address).
The field split follows the public Xenos `GPUTEXTURE_FETCH_CONSTANT` layout (Xenia `xenos.h`; from memory — every derived quantity is
checked against Studio's independently verified readings: width / height bytes, the `tiled` bit and pitch of `tdb-rx2::texlib`).

Per file: descriptors, their texture-data slot sizes (tag `00 01 00 31`), the name table. Census keys: (width, height, format, tiled, mips =
mip_max − mip_min + 1, dimension, packed_mips) → count, plus per-key the distinct values of every other field, so a writer can see which
fields are functions of the shape (pitch, base / mip addresses, DW11 / DW12 / DW13 bytes) and which are constant. Tests per descriptor:
`pitch == ceil(width / 32)`; `mip_address − base_address == tile-aligned base-mip size / 4096` (Studio's DW12 rule generalised);
`DW13 byte 2 == bit_length(max(width, height))`. Failures are kept with the file path.
Usage: python r32_rw4xb2_descriptor_census.py <out.json> [--titles nhl07,nhl11,...] [--max N]
